findings.body:
chunk 2/3:

When Adaptive Card handling fails, this sends HTTP 500 even though it constructs an invoke error envelope. Microsoft's [Universal Action Model contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/adaptive-cards/authoring-cards/universal-action-model#response-format) requires HTTP 200 for handled invokes, with the failure carried in the body's `statusCode`. Teams therefore receives a transport failure instead of the intended actionable error response. Use HTTP 200 for invoke error envelopes while retaining non-2xx responses for failed message saves, and correct the focused test that currently expects HTTP 500.
findings.title: Not done: Teams-compatible invoke failure responses

findings.body:
chunk 2/3:

Every connector failure becomes a plain Error without its status code. Consequently, a Microsoft 413 response cannot reach the existing payload-splitting retry contract demonstrated by the supplied `teams.test.ts` cases, so oversized messages fail instead of being split and delivered. Those tests inject 413 directly through a fake SDK and miss this loss at the new transport boundary. Preserve an allowlisted numeric status on the sanitized error and exercise the connector-to-channel failure path.
findings.title: Preserve safe provider status codes when sanitizing delivery errors
